source_text: Tamen ne quid negligenter praeteriisse videamur, accipe aliud. Hunc parturitionum dolorem compertum est pro parentium corporibus viribusque variari. Barbarorum certe feminae, et pastorum, quae exercitatione indurescunt, in mediis itineribus tanta facilitate pariunt, ut non intermisso viandi labore fetus suos procurent, et statim vehant, quae nihil pariendi difficultate marcentes, onera ventris ad humeros suos transferunt; et generaliter inopia vilium feminarum, operam obstetricum non requirit; at e regione locupletes deliciis molliuntur, et quo plures habuerit quaeque sollicitos, eo amplius et discit et gestit aegrescere, putatque se tantis egere, quantis abundat obsequiis. Maritorum sane divitum manus numquam in sentibus aerumnam primi hominis experitur; quin immo fidentes copiis, indignum se putant momentum aliquod votis fertilitatis impendere, extra formidinem etiam famis possessionum dilatatione sistentes, mandant aliquoties, ut ait poeta: Deiunge boves, dum tubera mittas [n179] . Si ergo et parientium dolor spectat ad instituta naturae, quod et brutorum exemplo animalium, et sententiae divinae proprietate perdoctum est; si interceptio fructuum, et exortus spinarum inter cetera quidem creatus est, personis tamen quibusdam factus est densior et molestior; si postremo, ut difficultas ipsa parientis, ita etiam glebarum spinositas pro corporibus regionibusque variatur; postremo, si perdurat ille angor post gratiam in visceribus feminarum, hunc vero opulentorum luxuries penitus ignorat; si resolutio corporis propter quid secutura esset, expressum est, et artibus magis quam erroribus applicata; apparet hic quoque Catholicorum veritati omnia consonare, nec quidquam vobis vel feminas prodesse, vel spinas.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless lest we seem to have passed anything negligently, receive another. This pain of parturitions has been found to vary according to the bodies and powers of parents. The females of barbarians certainly, and of shepherds, who grow hard by exercise, in the middle of journeys give birth with so great facility, that with the labor of traveling not interrupted they procure their offspring, and immediately carry, who languishing nothing by the difficulty of giving birth transfer the burdens of the belly to their own shoulders; and generally the poverty of cheap females does not require the work of midwives; but from the opposite side the rich are softened by delights, and by how many anxious people each has had, so much more she both learns and exults to grow sick, and thinks she needs as many as she abounds in obsequies. The hands of rich husbands indeed never experience in brambles the hardship of the first human; nay rather trusting in plenty, they think themselves unworthy to expend any moment on the wishes of fertility, standing even outside a fear of hunger by a dilatation of possessions, they command sometimes, as the poet says: Unyoke the oxen, while you send truffles. If therefore even the pain of those giving birth looks to the institutions of nature, which has been thoroughly taught both by the example of brute animals, and by the property of the divine sentence; if an interception of fruits, and an arising of thorns was created among the rest indeed, yet for certain persons was made denser and more troublesome; if finally, as the difficulty itself of the one giving birth, so also the thorniness of clods varies according to bodies and regions; finally, if that anguish endures after grace in the viscera of females, but this the luxury of the wealthy thoroughly ignores; if the resolution of the body on account of what it would be about to follow was expressed, and applied more to arts than to errors; it appears here also that all things agree with the truth of the Catholics, nor do either females or thorns profit you anything.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Yet lest we seem to have passed anything over carelessly, consider another point. Childbirth pain is known to vary with mothers’ bodies and strength. Women among foreign peoples and shepherds, hardened by exertion, give birth during journeys with such ease that they tend and immediately carry their offspring without interrupting the labor of travel. Not exhausted by childbirth’s difficulty, they transfer the womb’s burden to their shoulders. Generally, poor women’s lack of resources requires no midwives’ services. By contrast, wealthy women are softened by luxury: the more attendants each has, the more she learns and desires to be ill, and she thinks she needs as many services as she has available.

The hands of wealthy husbands certainly never experience the first human’s misery among thorns. Confident in their resources and placed beyond fear even of hunger by extensive estates, they consider it beneath them to spend a moment wishing for fertility. Sometimes, as the poet says, they order: ‘Unyoke the oxen, provided you send truffles’ (Genesis 3:16–19) (Juvenal, Satires 5.119).

If, then, women’s childbirth pain belongs to nature’s arrangements, as shown both by irrational animals’ example and the precise divine pronouncement; if withholding of fruit and the rise of thorns were created among other things but made denser and more troublesome for particular people; if childbirth’s difficulty and soil’s thorniness vary with bodies and regions; if the former pang continues in women’s inward parts after grace, while wealthy luxury knows nothing of the latter; and if the reason bodily dissolution would follow was expressly stated and attached to the manner of making rather than to errors—then here too everything plainly agrees with catholic truth. Neither women nor thorns help you at all.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
